contivoAi.h1Post: — how artificial intelligence changes the work of an accounting firm
contivoAi.lead: AI accounting is an approach where artificial intelligence takes over the most repetitive part of accounting work: it reads documents, codes them and posts them, while a human approves and makes the decisions. Below we explain what an AI accounting program is, how it works and what it really changes in an accounting firm.

sections.title: What AI-based accounting is
sections.body: A traditional accounting program is a tool in which the accountant does everything manually. An accounting program with AI goes further: an artificial intelligence model understands the content of documents and proposes postings on its own, flags errors and answers regulatory questions. AI in accounting does not replace the accountant — it takes over routine and gives back time for knowledge work.

sections.title: How AI posts a document — step by step

points.d: AI reads an invoice or document from an email or scan — line items, amounts, the counterparty, tax ID.
The model proposes a posting to the right accounts, following the chart of accounts and the firm’s practice.
The document is matched to the right client and accounting period.
The accountant approves or corrects with one click — the rest happens automatically.

sections.title: What an accounting firm gains with AI

points.d: Repetitive postings and retyping data from invoices disappear.
The same team serves more companies because AI handles the routine.
AI catches unusual amounts, missing documents and upcoming deadlines.
The AI assistant knows the current legal state — VAT, PIT, CIT, KSeF, JPK.

sections.title: An accounting program with AI — this is what Contivo does
sections.body: Contivo is the first Polish accounting system designed from the ground up around artificial intelligence (AI-Native). AI reads and posts documents, the assistant answers regulatory questions, and the system tracks KSeF, JPK, ZUS and tax-return deadlines. All in one cloud platform — with code, hosting and data in Poland.

contivoAi.faqTitle: Frequently asked questions about AI accounting

faq.q: Will artificial intelligence replace the accountant?
faq.a: No. AI takes over repetitive routine — reading and posting documents — while the accountant approves, decides and handles matters that require expertise. It is a tool that boosts productivity, not a replacement for a person.

faq.q: Is AI accounting safe?
faq.a: In Contivo, yes — code, hosting and data stay in Poland, and the system is GDPR-compliant. Documents are not sent abroad.

faq.q: Is an AI accounting program compliant with Polish regulations?
faq.a: Yes. Contivo natively supports KSeF, generates JPK_V7, JPK_KR and JPK_FA and handles ZUS, and the AI assistant knows the current legal state.

faq.q: How do I start with AI accounting?
faq.a: The easiest way is to try a ready system. Contivo supports taking over a company from your current program, including importing HR data and historical settlements.

faq.q: How is Mimi different from Siri?
faq.a: Mimi is designed for Polish: it understands inflection, Polish dates and natural sentences rather than a list of commands. It does not replace Siri — it works alongside it, as a separate app that you open or start by voice in the car.

faq.q: Do I need an Anthropic account?
faq.a: Yes. Mimi uses the Claude model on your own API key, so you pay for actual usage instead of a subscription with a margin on top. Creating an account and generating a key takes a few minutes, and the app walks you through it step by step.

faq.q: How much does it cost to use?
faq.a: You buy the app once in the App Store. For understanding your commands you pay Anthropic directly — with daily use that is usually a few zlotys a month. We take no commission on that and we do not see your bills.

faq.q: Does Mimi work without the internet?
faq.a: Wake-word listening and speech recognition can work offline, but understanding a command requires a connection to the Claude model. Without the internet Mimi says plainly that it cannot answer right now.

faq.q: What exactly do you send to Anthropic?
faq.a: The content of the command and the context of the last few utterances. If you ask about a contact, a route or an email, the request may include the data needed to carry it out. Readings from the Health app are excluded from this and never leave the device.

faq.q: Does Mimi read my messages and emails?
faq.a: No. Mimi helps you write and send them, but it does not browse your inbox or your conversation history. Telegram is the exception: if you buy that integration and connect your own bot, Mimi will read out messages sent to that bot when you ask.

faq.q: What is the Telegram integration?
faq.a: It is an add-on on a monthly subscription. It lets you send and receive messages through your own Telegram bot without opening the app — mainly useful in the car. Opening chats and Telegram calls work without a subscription.

faq.q: How do I delete my data?
faq.a: In Mimi's Settings, under “Your data”, a single command erases the conversation history, notes, settings and the API key and tokens. We make it a separate button because Keychain entries on their own survive uninstalling the app.

sections.h: 2. Data sent to Anthropic (the Claude model)
body: In order to understand a command, Mimi sends to Anthropic's API (api.anthropic.com) the content of your command — typed or converted from speech to text — the context of the last few utterances in the conversation, and the current date and time, so that “tomorrow” or “in two hours” are understood correctly.

If the command concerns a specific person or place, that context may include the data necessary to carry it out: the name and phone number of the contact found, the recipient's email address, the name of the destination or your approximate location. The scope is limited to what is needed to execute the command.

Requests are sent on your own Anthropic API key, which you create and enter in the app yourself. You settle payments with Anthropic directly, and your data is subject to Anthropic's privacy policy and terms. Codentra has no access to the content of your requests or to your Anthropic account.

Speech-to-text conversion is performed by the speech recognition built into iOS. Depending on your settings and the capabilities of the device, it happens on the device or on Apple's servers. Mimi does not store audio recordings.

In Mimi's Settings you can turn on the “On-device speech recognition only” option — the recording then does not leave the phone. Listening for the wake word (“Mimi”, “hey Mimi”) always runs on the device only.

sections.h: 4. Data that does not leave the device
body: The following data is processed locally only and is not sent anywhere:
list: Health and activity data from the Health app (steps, heart rate, calories burned, workouts). Readings are shown and read out loud on the device only; they do not go to the language model or anywhere else.
Notes saved in Mimi — stored in the app's local database.
Photos — Mimi opens the camera or the system photo library; images are not transmitted to anyone.
Files and PDF documents created by Mimi — they stay in the app's directory on the device.
The API key, the Telegram bot token and Twilio credentials — stored in the device's Keychain, protected by iOS, with no copying to other devices.

sections.h: 5. Data passed to other services at your command
body: If you use these features, Mimi passes data directly to the services you designate yourself:
list: Telegram (a subscription feature) — the message content and the chat identifier go to the Telegram Bot API, on your own bot token.

Calls and text messages through Twilio (an optional feature, for advanced users) — the destination number and the message content go to Twilio, on an account belonging to you. Codentra is not an intermediary in the call or in its billing.
Text messages, iMessages and emails sent without these features go through the standard iOS system sheets — Mimi only fills them in, and you confirm the sending.
does not collect analytics data and contains no third-party libraries for analytics or advertising
does not track you across apps or websites
does not sell or share data for marketing purposes
does not build a user profile and does not make automated decisions producing legal effects

body: Processing takes place in order to perform the function you ask for — the basis is the performance of a contract (Article 6(1)(b) GDPR) and, as regards passing the content of a command to Anthropic, your consent (Article 6(1)(a) GDPR), given on first launch of the app. You can withdraw that consent at any time by deleting the API key in Settings or by uninstalling Mimi.

You have the right to access your data, to rectify it, to erase it, to restrict processing, to data portability and to object. Because Codentra does not store your data, you exercise these rights yourself on the device. That is what Mimi Settings → Your data → “Delete all Mimi data” is for: a single command erases the conversation history, all notes, settings and the API key and tokens from the Keychain. Uninstalling the app alone does not remove Keychain entries, which is why this option exists separately.

For matters concerning data on the side of Anthropic, Telegram or Twilio, turn to those entities respectively. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the President of the Personal Data Protection Office (ul. Stawki 2, 00-193 Warsaw).

sections.h: 8. Transfers of data outside the EEA
body: Anthropic, Telegram and Twilio process data on servers outside the European Economic Area, including in the United States. The transfer takes place on the basis of the mechanisms provided for by those entities in their own terms. If you do not want the content of your commands to leave the EEA, do not use Mimi — without access to the language model the app will not understand commands.

Codentra does not store data, so it sets no retention period for it. Data on the device stays there until you delete it. The conversation history lives only until the app is closed, and you can clear it with the bin icon. Notes, settings and keys are erased by the “Delete all Mimi data” option in Settings. Retention periods on the side of Anthropic, Telegram and Twilio are set by their own policies.
Mimi is not directed at children under 13 and does not knowingly collect their data.
We will announce material changes in the update notes in the App Store and through the update date at the top of this document.

topics.q: Mimi does not respond to commands
topics.a: Most often the API key is missing or has stopped working. Open Mimi Settings and tap “Check key” — the message tells you what is wrong. If the key was rejected, generate a new one at console.anthropic.com. Check too whether your Anthropic account has funds.

topics.q: Where to get an Anthropic API key
topics.a: Create an account at console.anthropic.com, go to API Keys and create a new key. Copy it straight away — it is shown only once. Then paste it into Mimi Settings and tap “Check key”.

topics.q: The microphone does not work or Mimi cannot hear
topics.a: In iOS Settings → Mimi, check whether access to the microphone and speech recognition has been granted. If it has and the problem remains, close the app and open it again — that releases the audio session held by another app.

topics.q: Listening for the “Mimi” wake word will not turn on
topics.a: Wake-word listening works offline only and requires the Polish dictation model to be downloaded. You download it in iOS Settings → General → Keyboard → Dictation. Listening works while the app is open, and in the car also while the phone is locked.

topics.q: Mimi gets dates and times wrong
topics.a: Speak in full sentences and give a reference point: “next Tuesday at ten” works better than just “Tuesday”. If the command is complex, switch to a stronger Claude model in Settings — it handles tricky dates noticeably better.

topics.q: The calendar, contacts or reminders do not work
topics.a: This is a matter of system permissions. iOS Settings → Mimi shows the list of granted access. Calendar and Reminders require full access, not write-only — otherwise Mimi cannot read existing entries.

In iOS Settings → General → CarPlay, check whether Mimi is on the list of apps visible on the car screen. Once the car is connected, Mimi starts listening for the wake word on its own — you can switch that off in Mimi Settings, under Speech.

You need your own bot: message @BotFather on Telegram, create a bot and copy the token into Mimi Settings. Then add contacts as name → chat_id pairs; you find your own chat_id by messaging @userinfobot. The recipient must send /start to your bot first. Automatic sending and reading require an active subscription.

topics.q: How to restore a subscription purchase
topics.a: In Mimi Settings, under Telegram, tap “Restore purchases”. The purchase is tied to your Apple ID, so it comes back after changing phones too — provided you sign in to the same account.

topics.q: How to delete all your data
topics.a: Mimi Settings → Your data → “Delete all Mimi data”. This erases the conversation history, notes, settings and the API key and tokens from the Keychain. We make it a separate button because Keychain entries survive uninstalling the app.

homeSeo.faqTitle: Frequently asked questions about working with Codentra

faq.q: What does Codentra do?
faq.a: Codentra is an AI software house based in Świdnica, Poland. We design and build custom software — web applications, SaaS platforms and internal tools — and implement AI-based solutions in businesses. We are the makers of Contivo, an AI accounting system for accounting firms.

faq.q: What is Contivo?
faq.a: Contivo is Codentra's own product — the first AI-native Polish accounting system for accounting firms, available at contivo.pl. AI reads and posts documents, and the system handles KSeF, JPK, ZUS DRA, HR and payroll and fixed assets in one cloud platform.

faq.q: Do you only work with companies in Poland?
faq.a: Our headquarters is in Świdnica, Poland, and we work with companies across the country. Most of our collaboration happens remotely, so location is rarely a constraint.

faq.q: How long does it take to build custom software?
faq.a: It depends on scope. We work iteratively: after discovery we deliver a working prototype of the product core within 2–3 weeks, then build out full functionality in short cycles with frequent releases.

faq.q: What does an AI implementation look like?
faq.a: We start by identifying processes where AI will have a measurable impact — such as document handling, answering customer questions or searching company knowledge. Then we build a prototype, measure answer quality and integrate the solution with your systems.

faq.q: Is company data safe during an AI implementation?
faq.a: Yes. We design GDPR-compliant solutions with control over where data is processed. We know Polish regulations — KSeF, JPK, ZUS — because we work with them every day in Contivo.

faq.q: Which technologies do you use?
faq.a: A modern web stack (including TypeScript, React and Next.js), cloud infrastructure with CI/CD, and large language models (LLMs) with techniques such as RAG, function calling and AI agents.

faq.q: Where should a company start with AI?
faq.a: With a single process that takes your team a lot of time and is repetitive — e.g. document handling or answering common questions. That's where results show fastest and ROI is easy to measure.

faq.q: Is an AI implementation GDPR-compliant?
faq.a: Yes, when designed properly. We choose model providers and architecture so you control where data is processed and limit access to sensitive information.

faq.q: Will AI replace employees?
faq.a: That's not the goal. AI takes over repetitive routine, while people approve results and focus on work that requires knowledge and judgement.

faq.q: Can you integrate AI with our existing system?
faq.a: Yes. We integrate language models with existing systems via APIs — without replacing your entire software stack.
